messages.subject: problem with geom_point and alpha
parts:
I am having a problem using alpha for some shapes in geom_point.

----
df=data.frame(x=sample(1:10, 10), y=sample(1:10,10))
ggplot(df) + geom_point(aes(x,y), shape=16, alpha=0.2)
# creates a point graph with the shape and alpha as expected.

ggplot(df) + geom_point(aes(x,y), shape=24, alpha=0.2)
# same here with the border correctly coloured.

ggplot(df) + geom_point(aes(x,y), shape=20, alpha=0.2)
# the symbols now have a ring without alpha applied and a somewhat bigger background with the alpha applied.
# same for shape 19

It is pretty old code i am using, so has there something been changed or is it a bug?


Thanks,
Herbert

messages.author: ff42271ef6191bca
messages.subject: Re: problem with geom_point and alpha
parts:
I took a deeper look at the issue.

df=data.frame(x=sample(20,20), y=sample(20,20), shape=factor(rep(c(16,17,19,20),5)))
ggplot(df) + geom_point(aes(x,y,shape=shape), size=10, alpha=0.2) + scale_shape_manual(values=c(16,17,19,20))

The code creates a simple graph with the shapes 16, 17, 19 and 20. After saving as pdf on my OS-X system i inspected the file.

Using "preview" the shape 19 and 20 have a darker ring like a border. In Adobe Acrobat the same shapes show like rectangles with round corners.
In Adobe Illustrator the shape 16 is just a circle, while the shape 19 has a border, which, after ungrouping, shows darker than the circle.

Looks like a complex problem including ggsave (or generally savong graphics as pdf) and the graphics design for the shapes 19 and 20.
I attache some jpgs which are screen shots for illustration.

So how to fix it?

Thanks,
Herbert

messages.subject: Re: problem with geom_point and alpha
parts:
This is a known feature of grid. For shapes with both stroke and fill,
they're drawn separately, and the alpha affects both. I was puzzled by
this too, so I checked with Paul Murrell.

Hadley
